I586.best_result: DistilBERT + XLM-RoBERTa late fusion accuracy 76.68%; weighted F1 76.54%
I586.summary_en: Proposes a multilingual text-based screening framework for depression, anxiety and stress that fuses DistilBERT and XLM-RoBERTa at the logit level, with an interpretability pipeline and an LLM module for non-clinical guidance. The fused model reaches 76.68% accuracy (weighted F1 76.54%); the dataset and population are not described.

I587.screening_reason: Sports training assessment, not mental health
I587.summary_en: Proposes a CNN with a Logish activation function to evaluate modern sports training of college students from training videos. It reports 99.52% accuracy, outperforming CNN and VEVF.

I588.screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance, not mental health
I588.summary_en: Predicts student academic performance from 10,000 student records with Graph Attention Networks and BiLSTM-Attention, explained with GNNExplainer and Integrated Gradients. BiLSTM-Attention performs best (R2 0.988), with study hours, past scores and extracurricular activities as influential features.

I589.summary_en: Presents a bilingual AI chatbot for rural students that combines textual, spoken and facial emotional cues to detect sadness, anxiety, distress and suicidal risk and recommend culturally appropriate interventions, alerting parents or teachers in emergencies. No data or evaluation results are reported.

I590.summary_en: Proposes an active learning framework with RNN, LSTM and GRU for detecting student anxiety, iteratively retraining on high-uncertainty samples to reduce dependence on labeled data. No dataset or performance results are reported.

I591.summary_en: Develops classification models for personalized premenstrual symptom and depressive crisis risk tracking in 282 female volunteers from the University of Phayao using six algorithms (DT, KNN, LR, NB, RF, SVM) with 10-fold cross-validation. Performance is described as high but no figures are given.

I592.summary_en: Proposes an online stress analysis and management tool for students that integrates OpenAI GPT-3.5 with NoSQL databases to provide personalized recommendations. No evaluation data or results are reported.

I593.screening_reason: Sports performance and physical fitness, not mental health
I593.summary_en: Discusses data mining-based sports performance management and physical fitness analysis systems for athletes using sensor data. No specific data, method or results are reported.

I594.summary_en: Detects stress and fatigue levels of university students in online classes with a hybrid CNN-LSTM using facial expressions, voice tone and keystroke dynamics. It achieves 92.3% accuracy, outperforming SVM and Random Forest.

I595.summary_en: Forecasts loneliness seven days in advance in college students using wearable (smart ring, watch) physiological data and smartphone behavioral data with personalized machine learning models. It reaches 0.82 accuracy and F1, with Shapley values used for explainability.

I596.screening_reason: Main outcome is eligibility for academic pathway; mental health is a predictor
I596.summary_en: Analyzes how academic performance, mental health and gender relate to vocational college students' eligibility for the specialized-to-bachelor pathway using six neural networks (GRU, LSTM, BiLSTM, etc.). Academic achievement is the main predictor, while mental health acts indirectly through academic performance.

I597.summary_en: Systematic review of 35 studies on intelligent stress detection in higher education students, covering data sources, machine learning techniques and validation. It reports Random Forest accuracies up to 95% and superior CNN performance with multimodal data, while noting reliance on survey data and privacy and generalizability issues.

I598.summary_en: Presents SOFIA, a multimodal emotion detection system for high school students combining deep learning with interactive hardware (plush toy and digital interface). It reports 95% emotion detection accuracy, 97% engagement and 85% of users reporting improved emotional understanding.

I599.screening_reason: Main outcome is dropout; mental health only in counselling module
I599.best_result: Random Forest best overall accuracy (no figure reported)
I599.summary_en: Proposes an AI-based dropout prediction and counselling system combining behavioral, academic and socio-economic factors, trained on a synthetic dataset of 70,000 student records, with SHAP explanations and personalized academic and mental health support suggestions. Random Forest achieves the best overall accuracy, without figures reported.

I600.screening_reason: General physical health and disease prevention, not mental health
I600.summary_en: Designs an information system for assessing student health and preventing disease using artificial intelligence algorithms, aimed at educational institutions in Kazakhstan. No data, specific method or results are reported.

I601.screening_reason: Title refers to IT professionals while abstract refers to students; no method or results
I601.summary_en: Proposes estimating students' stress levels from a Google Form survey on psychological factors during COVID-19 using a machine learning model. The model, sample and results are not described, and the title refers to IT professionals.

I602.screening_reason: Physical fitness and BMI, not mental health
I602.summary_en: Evaluates the effect of 12 weeks of intelligent rope skipping on BMI and physical fitness in 60 overweight middle school students using cubic, S and logistic regression. Training improved BMI, cardiopulmonary function and strength.

I603.screening_reason: Mixed population; only one of three datasets involves students
I603.summary_en: Compares XGBoost, Random Forest, LightGBM and SVM for predicting stress and sleep disorders on three datasets (Sleep Health and Lifestyle, Stress Detection, Student Lifestyle). Ensemble models perform best: RF 74% on stress detection, XGBoost 90% on sleep health and LightGBM 98% on student lifestyle.

I604.summary_en: Classifies intentional and accidental opioid users among 455 patients from the MIMIC-III database using machine learning and deep learning with attention and knowledge distillation. It reaches 95% accuracy on structured data, 64% on unstructured data and 76.44% with the distilled integrated model.

I605.best_result: Decision Tree and Random Forest accuracy 95%
I605.summary_en: Classifies game addiction among digital-native students using Random Forest, SVM, Decision Tree and Naive Bayes with Borderline-SMOTE for class imbalance. Decision Tree and Random Forest perform best with 95% accuracy.

I606.screening_reason: No analytical or data mining method described
I606.summary_en: Examines academic, relational, economic and social factors affecting the happiness of Sri Lankan university students and proposes a support application. Preliminary results indicate that social support, academic success, financial security and mental health resources contribute to well-being; data and methods are not described.

I607.summary_en: Proposes an attention-based explainable method (self-attention and graph attention layers) to classify positive and negative affect from wearable multivariate time series collected from 21 college students over one year. It achieves 78.62% accuracy for positive affect and 76.30% for negative affect, with temporal and modality-level explanations.

I608.summary_en: Proposes a system that analyzes recorded videos of students in remote learning to assess their engagement and emotional states using machine learning. No dataset or quantitative results are reported.

I609.summary_en: Classifies five anxiety levels from narrative DAAS questionnaire responses of students at Universitas Lancang Kuning, Indonesia, using TF-IDF, SMOTE, Random Forest, C4.5 and Naive Bayes combined by voting ensembles. Hard Voting performs best (accuracy 0.89, macro F1 0.89).

I610.screening_reason: Web platform and encryption design without data analytics or AI
I610.summary_en: Describes the implementation of a student psychological mutual aid platform on the Symfony MVC architecture with data encryption. Testing is reported to show the platform is efficient, without analytical data or results.

I611.screening_reason: Outcome is sleep disorder risk; population includes instructors
I611.summary_en: Investigates the association between LMS engagement and sleep disorder risk among students and instructors during COVID-19 using educational data mining on Moodle logs and box-plot outlier detection. Some students and instructors are identified as potentially experiencing sleep disorders.

I612.screening_reason: General social media users, not students
I612.summary_en: Applies NLP and deep learning (Transformers) to social media texts to detect personality traits and indicators of psychological disorders such as depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder. Deep learning outperforms traditional text classification, without figures reported.

I613.screening_reason: Calorie management and nutrition, not mental health
I613.summary_en: Proposes Eat4U, a mobile application for university students in metropolitan Lima that uses Mask R-CNN instance segmentation to estimate meal calories and recommend healthier options. The fine-tuned model reaches a mean IoU of 86%.

I614.screening_reason: AI in education management, not mental health
I614.summary_en: Describes an education big data collection and analysis platform and an intelligent education management system for primary and secondary schools. No data or results are reported.

I615.screening_reason: Outcome is sleep quality, not directly mental health
I615.summary_en: Predicts sleep quality (PSQI) in university students from demographic, lifestyle, psychosocial and environmental variables with machine learning models. XGBoost performs best (F1 0.9544, accuracy 0.9366), and SHAP identifies financial stress, pain, sleep environment and bedtime habits as key factors.

I616.summary_en: Develops a web-based depression risk assessment system using the Thai CES-D and association rule mining, tested with 400 students from Phetchaburi Rajabhat University. 27.5% of students were at risk, with higher risk among third-year students, off-campus residents, students from divorced families and females.

I617.screening_reason: Focus on instructional design with qualitative analysis; no data analytics method described
I617.summary_en: Proposes an emotionally responsive AI co-regulation framework for K-12 classrooms, developed through design-based research with 12 teachers and 240 students using a dashboard of engagement and emotion cues and mixed-methods data. Findings suggest emotionally aware AI can enhance teacher reflexivity and student agency.

I618.screening_reason: Data from general social media, not specifically students
I618.summary_en: Detects depression-related sentiment linked to COVID-19 in over 200,000 tweets and public forum posts using NLP and an LSTM, intended for student communication platforms. The LSTM achieves 88% accuracy.

I619.summary_en: Classifies students' stress levels from social media behavior and academic attributes using RF, SVM, KNN, LR, XGBoost and a feedforward neural network. Performance is described as notable but no figures are given.

I620.screening_reason: Infectious disease health education, not mental health
I620.summary_en: Evaluates an IoT- and AI-enabled health education framework on students' infectious disease prevention knowledge and behavior using multiple linear regression and difference-in-differences analysis. The intervention is reported to improve knowledge, attitudes and practices.

I621.screening_reason: Main outcome is dropout risk; anxiety is a predictor
I621.best_result: XGBoost higher F1 than RF (no figure reported)
I621.summary_en: Predicts higher-education non-enrollment risk among secondary school graduates in Libya's Fezzan region with Random Forest and XGBoost, using composite indices including stress-anxiety, SMOTE and LASSO feature selection. XGBoost outperforms RF, and LIME shows high anxiety increases dropout risk.

I622.best_result: CatBoost+GB stacking accuracy 80.7%, AUC 0.757 (PHQ-9>=10); AdaBoost+LR stacking AUC 0.762 (PHQ-9>=15)
I622.summary_en: Predicts depression (PHQ-9) at two thresholds in an open dataset of 1,919 Bangladeshi college-going adolescents with 35 classical, ensemble, deep learning and stacking models. CatBoost+GradientBoosting stacking reaches 80.7% accuracy (AUC 0.757) at the moderate threshold and AdaBoost+LR AUC 0.762 at the severe threshold; family unrest is the most influential predictor.

I623.screening_reason: Outcome is cognitive function and meditative state, not mental health
I623.summary_en: Classifies cognitive function states (low vs better) from PEBL cognitive task scores of 54 college students before and after Yoga and Rajyog meditation using a CNN. The model achieves 74% accuracy and 75% F1.

I624.screening_reason: Focus on learning behavior monitoring, not mental health
I624.summary_en: Proposes a machine learning framework with spatiotemporal features and attention mechanisms to detect student behaviors such as yawning and nail-biting in virtual learning environments, linked to smart city applications. It reports superior accuracy and F1 on benchmark datasets without figures.

I625.screening_reason: Population not specified as students; no data or results
I625.summary_en: Proposes an HTM-based VAE-GAN model to identify relationships between musical features and mental health features. No data, population or results are reported.

I626.screening_reason: General review of mental health conversational agents, not focused on students
I626.summary_en: Surveys computational agents (chatbots and social robots) for delivering internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy, along with datasets, models (CNN, RNN, HAN, Transformers) and evaluation metrics. It is motivated by rising mental health problems among youth and students.

I627.summary_en: Presents ZenithMind, a MERN-stack mental health assistant for college students that uses Google Fit data (steps, sleep, mood) to provide a CBT chatbot, mood, anxiety and stress dashboards and relaxation modules. No evaluation results are reported.

I628.screening_reason: Outcome is learning focus; mood is only a predictor
I628.summary_en: Analyzes factors influencing learning focus (sleep duration, lunch, study duration, mood) among students at the Republic of Indonesia Defense University using Decision Tree, Random Forest, Logistic Regression and SVM. Random Forest achieves the highest accuracy (71%), with sleep and study duration as main factors.

I629.summary_en: Predicts psychological resilience risk in medical students from eye-tracking pupil diameter features under auditory and visual stimuli, using RFECV and LR, RF, SVM and XGBoost. SVM performs best (balanced accuracy 0.906, AUC 0.932), and SHAP shows auditory stimuli are more informative.

I630.screening_reason: Outcome is physical exercise, not mental health
I630.summary_en: Analyzes the influence of screen time on daily exercise in one male college student using smartphone and tablet screen time, steps, sleep score and weather data with GBDT. Total screen time, smartphone screen time and sleep score are the most important variables.

I631.screening_reason: Ethics teaching in machine learning courses, not mental health
I631.summary_en: Reports the experience of embedding ethics and gender content in undergraduate and master machine learning courses at the University of Santiago de Compostela. Students reflected on ethical and gender issues.

I632.summary_en: Predicts entrepreneurial competency of university students with XGBoost and LightGBM, compared with KNN, random forest and logistic regression. XGBoost achieves 79% accuracy, outperforming LightGBM (71%).

I633.summary_en: Proposes a two-stage machine learning framework for depression risk screening and severity evaluation in college students using demographic and environmental features. XGBoost reaches ROC-AUC 0.718 for detection, SHAP identifies living with parents, family finances and teacher relationship as key predictors, and severity evaluation reaches AUC 0.636 with 0.716 recall.

I634.summary_en: Presents EDU-SENSE, an AI-driven e-learning platform for primary school pupils preparing for Sri Lanka's Grade 5 Scholarship Examination that combines personalized content, stress detection and an emotion-aware chatbot using machine learning, NLP and fine-tuned LLMs. No data or evaluation results are reported.

I635.screening_reason: Elderly and disabled people, not students or mental health
I635.summary_en: Discusses the application of artificial intelligence to elderly care and the needs of elderly disabled people. No data, method or results are reported.

I636.summary_en: Predicts weekly ADHD symptom levels and diagnostic status from passively collected smartphone app usage data of 12 college-age students using a family of machine learning models. App usage features predict ADHD diagnostic status with F1 up to 0.88.

I637.screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance, not mental health
I637.summary_en: Examines the effect of class attendance discipline on student learning outcomes using attendance and grade records and simple linear regression. Attendance discipline explains 67% of the variance in the results quality index (R2 0.67).

I638.summary_en: Analyzes the relationship between sleep behaviors and self-reported physical and mental health problems using questionnaire responses from 1,022 Turkish university students and machine learning techniques. Patterns linking poor sleep to health problems are identified, without quantitative results reported.

I639.summary_en: Proposes an emotion-aware framework combining BERT-W word embeddings with BiLSTM-Attention to detect early psychological risk signals in social media texts from university students. The model outperforms existing machine learning methods in accuracy and robustness, without figures reported.

I640.summary_en: Detects behavioral health challenges (depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder) in high school students from time series of course grades using a deep encoder and a classifier that labels students as stable, monitor or critical. The model achieves a 93% weighted F1 score.

I641.screening_reason: Campus safety management, not mental health
I641.summary_en: Proposes a campus safety management system based on telecom big data and data fusion, with an algorithm predicting student behavior intent. It reports better accuracy and F1 than traditional algorithms, without figures.

I642.screening_reason: Physical health biochemical indices, not mental health
I642.summary_en: Builds a student biochemical index monitoring system based on K-means cluster analysis to inform students' physical health planning. The work describes the model, database and software design without results.

I643.summary_en: Proposes detecting students' emotions during examinations from handwriting features (pressure, slant, pen lift, speed, spacing) extracted from scanned exam sheets using image processing and machine learning. No data or results are reported.

I644.screening_reason: Outcome is sleep; synthetic data analyzed with descriptive statistics
I644.summary_en: Explores correlations between sleep patterns and lifestyle factors (screen time, caffeine, physical activity, study hours) in a synthetic dataset of 500 university student records using correlation and visualization techniques. Screen time and caffeine are negatively associated with sleep quality, while physical activity is positively associated.

I645.summary_en: Proposes a two-stage framework combining a Temporal Attention Model and a context-aware autoencoder to detect anomalous smartphone usage affecting digital well-being, trained on usage logs of university students in Coimbatore. It achieves 98.2% accuracy and 97.5% F1, outperforming standard classifiers.

I646.screening_reason: Physical health of elementary students, not mental health
I646.summary_en: Analyzes 2020 physical health data of elementary students (7-12 years) at Huayang Elementary School, Guangzhou, compared with 2014 national means using mathematical statistics. Body shape indexes are below the national mean while most physical functions exceed it.

I647.summary_en: Examines socioeconomic determinants of mental health in 10,000 students using academic, family income, social and psychological data. Low-income students show 23% higher stress; logistic regression classifies stress with 82.4% accuracy and XGBoost and SVM reach 99.8%, with academic performance, sleep and income as main predictors.

I648.summary_en: Predicts students' stress levels from a dataset based on standard measures using linear regression, Random Forest, SVM, Gradient Boosting and KNN. Random Forest Regressor performs best (MSE 0.1292, R2 0.8065), while Gradient Boosting is robust for stress category classification.

I649.summary_en: Proposes SABER, a hybrid stress detection system for youth from social media and physiological data using Naive Bayes, Random Forest, SVM, Logistic Regression and Decision Tree, improved with stacking, text augmentation and BERT embeddings. Ensemble and transformer-based approaches outperform traditional models, without figures reported.

I650.screening_reason: Focus on cyberbullying detection; students not the explicit population
I650.summary_en: Presents BulliShield, an application that extracts text from screenshots of conversations via OCR and detects hate speech in Bangla and English with machine and deep learning, supporting complaint handling by authorities and AI-based counseling. No evaluation results are reported.

I651.screening_reason: General population across age groups, not students
I651.summary_en: Predicts suicidal tendency across age groups from sociodemographic, clinical, behavioral and psychiatric data using five machine learning algorithms. SVM and Decision Tree perform best (accuracy 0.89), followed by Random Forest (0.84), KNN (0.81) and Gaussian Naive Bayes (0.53).

I652.summary_en: Classifies anxiety levels in nine engineering students (18-21 years) from EEG recorded with an EMOTIV EPOC+ during anxiety-inducing activities, using Wilcoxon and Mann-Whitney tests and machine learning with SAM labels. Random Forest and XGBoost achieve 72.27% accuracy.

I653.screening_reason: General review of anxiety detection, not focused on students
I653.summary_en: Literature review of studies applying machine learning to detect anxiety, categorized by methodology and data type (voice, facial expressions, heart rate, blood tests, brain imaging).

I654.summary_en: Analyzes students' mental condition during COVID-19 through sentiment analysis with NLTK on thoughts collected from the student community, displayed in a Flask web application. No sample size or results are reported.

I655.best_result: BVP + TEMP true positive rate up to 0.90 (median threshold)
I655.summary_en: Detects state anxiety (STAI-6) in STEM university students from wearable physiological signals (EDA, BVP, HRV, skin temperature) and speech using machine learning with clinical and median thresholds. BVP combined with skin temperature performs best, with true positive rates up to 0.90.

I656.summary_en: Designs ARU, a privacy-preserving automated stress monitoring system for Indian undergraduate students that collects physiological, social and behavioral data from smartphones and low-cost wearables and provides machine learning-driven insights validated with PSS and DSI. No evaluation results are reported.

I657.summary_en: Identifies student depression from cyber-activity patterns using Heterogeneous Graph Attention Networks trained on a Kaggle dataset. The model achieves 96.8% accuracy, 95.4% precision, 94.7% recall and 98.3% AUC-ROC.

I658.summary_en: Evaluates guided deep breathing and Indian classical music for exam anxiety in 60 undergraduate engineering students randomized to intervention and control groups, using GSR and HRV during the MIST task, non-parametric tests and machine learning. Both interventions reduce physiological arousal, and stress-state classifiers exceed 98% accuracy.

I659.best_result: Stacking with Gaussian Naive Bayes meta learner accuracy 95%
I659.summary_en: Detects student stress levels in Indonesia from DASS questionnaire data using Bernoulli, Gaussian and Multinomial Naive Bayes in a stacking framework with SMOTE. The Gaussian Naive Bayes meta learner achieves the best accuracy (95%).

I660.summary_en: Compares Random Forest and XGBoost for sentiment classification of anonymized student social media posts during pre-board exams, using slang normalization and TF-IDF. XGBoost outperforms RF on all metrics with 88.9% accuracy.

I661.summary_en: Detects depression from profile information collected through a survey of undergraduates, using NLP, machine learning and feature selection (mRMR, RFE, Boruta, LASSO). AdaBoost reaches 94% accuracy with all features and 96% with mRMR and Optuna tuning.

I662.summary_en: Proposes SLA-GF, an adaptive multi-layer feature fusion sentiment model based on the SKEP pre-trained model with inter-layer attention and gating, to analyze emotional polarity in higher education student feedback. On the SMILE-College dataset it outperforms baselines in accuracy and macro-F1, without figures reported.

I663.summary_en: Proposes an AI-driven university counselor work management system that predicts student performance and at-risk individuals from the UCI Student Performance Dataset with a hybrid ensemble tuned by Bayesian and Optuna optimization. The model exceeds 98.7% accuracy.

I664.summary_en: Classifies stress versus no stress from speech signals of International Islamic University Malaysia students using MFCC features, pause count and maximum amplitude with a neural network. No performance figures are reported.

I665.summary_en: Predicts smartphone addiction levels in 569 engineering students from behavioral (screen time, app usage) and psychological (Big Five) traits with a Random Forest classifier. It achieves 96% accuracy, with feature importance and LIME explaining predictions.

I666.screening_reason: Adolescent Twitter users, not clearly students; no results
I666.summary_en: Plans to detect depression in adolescents' Twitter posts by comparing machine learning algorithms with and without NLP. No data size or results are reported.

I667.screening_reason: Text analysis methods, not mental health or students
I667.summary_en: Describes LDA topic modelling and co-occurrence semantic network analysis, their applications and research progress.

I668.screening_reason: Cognitive level profiling, not mental health
I668.summary_en: Profiles cognitive levels of university students from 36,830 psychometric records using Spectral Clustering with optional IRT estimation. Silhouette, Calinski-Harabasz and Davies-Bouldin indices indicate satisfactory high, medium and low cognitive clusters.

I669.screening_reason: Physical disease diagnosis, not mental health
I669.summary_en: Designs an interpretable rule-based diagnostic system for six common diseases among university students, incorporating NLP and OpenAI GPT-3. No evaluation results are reported.

I670.screening_reason: Main outcome is academic grades; stress signals are predictors
I670.summary_en: Predicts student exam grades from a public wearable dataset of electrodermal activity, skin temperature and heart rate using Decision Tree, CNN, KNN, Random Forest and SVR regressors. No performance results are reported.

I671.screening_reason: General review of emotion AI across domains, not focused on student mental health
I671.summary_en: Reviews Emotion AI across education, the workplace and psychiatry, covering surveillance, privacy, emotional labor, machine learning versus deep learning models and ethical considerations for educational technology.

I672.summary_en: Examines relationships between digital well-being, digital hoarding and mobile information security awareness in 466 Faculty of Education students at Firat University using validated scales, descriptive analysis and association rules. Students show high digital well-being and moderate security awareness and digital hoarding.

I673.summary_en: Proposes predicting student academic emotions from facial expressions and body language using CNN and ResNet models to help teachers adapt instruction. No dataset size or performance results are reported.

I674.summary_en: Examines how AI/ML-related stress affects job satisfaction in 152 business school faculty using a survey and multiple regression. Task complexity stress and job security concerns reduce satisfaction, while self-efficacy increases it and buffers stress.

I675.screening_reason: Descriptive survey; machine learning only proposed as part of an intervention model
I675.summary_en: Examines the effects of digital pornography on 1,500 students at Chinhoyi University of Technology, Zimbabwe, using a survey including the mCIUS scale. Porn use is reported to negatively affect mental health (63.9%) and social relationships (58.7%), and an 8-way reduction model with a machine learning-based SMS warning engine is proposed.

I676.summary_en: Classifies occupational stress biomarkers among EFL teachers in higher education using hybrid deep learning models (CNN-SVM, VAE-RNN, CNN-RNN, CRNN-LSTM). CRNN-LSTM performs best with 95.53% accuracy.

I677.summary_en: Presents a personalized stress detection system for university students using wearable data from the public WESAD dataset, fine-tuning a baseline XGBoost model per individual through transfer learning. Personalized models consistently outperform the baseline, e.g. F1 increasing from 0.84 to 0.95.

I678.summary_en: Proposes an emotion-aware persuasive architecture that infers students' emotions from Empatica E4 physiological data to identify challenging classroom situations and send multimodal notifications, implemented as the Kusisqa system. Preliminary results indicate increased teacher awareness and perceived usefulness.

I679.summary_en: Proposes detecting stressed or depressed students from campus CCTV using facial and speech feature fusion with CLAHE enhancement, trained on the RAVDESS dataset. The proposed deep learning (MTCNN-based) model reaches 0.856 accuracy, outperforming SVM (0.791), Random Forest and Gradient Boosting.

I680.screening_reason: Indian women, not students; no analytical method described
I680.summary_en: Analyzes the effects of menarche, menstruation and menopause transition on stress and mood in 219 Indian women through a Google Forms survey. Age, weight and occupation influence stress and mood, with greater symptom severity in high-stress occupations.

I681.summary_en: Proposes an integrated model combining a facial emotion recognition CNN with Random Forest and AdaBoost to classify university students' academic stress as low, medium or high from emotional and behavioral data (GPA, social support, sleep, digital behavior). No performance figures are reported.

I682.screening_reason: Mixed datasets; only one from students; partly incoherent abstract
I682.summary_en: Compares five deep learning models (NN, LSTM, RNN, TabNet, CNN) for multiclass depression and anxiety classification on three datasets, one from student surveys. LSTM gives the highest accuracy on two datasets and CNN on the third, without figures reported.

I683.screening_reason: Assistive teaching technology for special education, not mental health
I683.summary_en: Presents GestuLearn, an interactive learning system using real-time hand tracking and gesture recognition with computer vision and machine learning for students with disabilities. No evaluation results are reported.

I684.screening_reason: People in their twenties; students not explicitly stated; no results
I684.summary_en: Designs a DSM-5-based multi-label classification method to predict depressive disorders in people in their twenties using data from the Everytime platform and a gated recurrent unit. No performance results are reported.

I685.best_result: AUC-ROC 91.60% (stress, with signal quality and questionnaires); 71.58% (fatigue)
I685.summary_en: Proposes a lightweight PPG processing pipeline to classify stress and fatigue in adolescent students using a wearable and app (Wellby) over one month, first evaluated on WESAD and AKTIVES. On Wellby data it reaches AUC-ROC of 77.02% for stress and 71.58% for fatigue, improving to 91.60% for stress with signal quality and baseline well-being questionnaires.

I686.summary_en: Formulates early depression detection from social media as a multiple-instance learning task, evaluated with transformer and LSTM architectures on a dataset of Brazilian university students. The approach yields better accuracy and explanation capabilities than previous methods, without figures reported.

I687.screening_reason: Online child grooming prevention, not student mental health
I687.summary_en: Develops a multilingual web application at the Technical University of Kosice to assess online conversations for signs of child grooming, vulgarity or blackmail. Testing results from users are presented.

I688.summary_en: Develops a multiclass stress classification framework for higher education students during Emergency Remote Learning from a novel questionnaire on psychosocial, environmental, pedagogical and demographic stressors, evaluating eight models with nested cross-validation. Logistic Regression performs best (93.67% accuracy, MCC 0.915), and XAI techniques identify reduced peer interaction and emotional disconnect as key stressors.

I689.screening_reason: Classical statistical analysis only, no data mining or machine learning
I689.summary_en: Examines associations between sleep quality, sleep control and depressive symptoms in 971 undergraduate students from the ANSWERS study using PSQI, CESD and BRISC with correlations, t-tests and ANOVA. Poor sleep correlates with depressive symptoms (r = 0.46), and greater perceived sleep control is associated with fewer symptoms.

I690.summary_en: Predicts college faculty attrition from salary, job satisfaction and institutional factors using logistic regression, decision tree, SVM, random forest, XGBoost and AdaBoost in an ensemble framework. High precision and recall are reported without figures.

I691.screening_reason: General student affairs management; mental health is only one function; no data
I691.summary_en: Explores an intelligent decision support system for university counselors using cloud computing, big data and AI for student behavior prediction, personalized counseling suggestions and management decisions, including mental health counseling. Efficiency improvements are reported without data.

I692.screening_reason: Outcome is sleep quality, not directly mental health
I692.summary_en: Applies causal machine learning (causal discovery and inference) to wearable data on sleep, physical activity and HRV from college students before and after the COVID-19 lockdown. The pandemic worsened sleep scores by 8%, with HRV and physical activity as mediators.

I693.screening_reason: Focus on learning outcomes and campus operations; welfare only one scenario
I693.summary_en: Proposes a theoretical AI-IoT smart campus framework evaluated in scenarios of adaptive learning, student engagement and welfare monitoring, and energy-space optimization. It reports efficient personalized support without empirical metrics.

I694.summary_en: Analyzes the impact of AI-based instructional technologies on the self-efficacy of 128 business educators using supervised machine learning. Random Forest achieves the highest accuracy (85.4), with prior digital exposure and frequency of use as key determinants.

I695.summary_en: Predicts depression among university students with Random Forest, XGBoost, Extra Trees, Gradient Boosting and LightGBM, and a stacked XGBoost + LightGBM model. The stacked model outperforms individual classifiers, with academic pressure and history of suicidal thoughts as top predictors; no figures are reported.

I696.screening_reason: Adults aged 18 and over, not specifically students
I696.summary_en: Classifies depression and anxiety from numerical responses of 4,184 individuals aged 18 and over diagnosed by a French university, using SMOTE, Random Forest feature selection and KNN, Random Forest and SVM with 10-fold cross-validation. Random Forest performs best, without figures reported.

I697.screening_reason: Outcome is school discipline and suspensions, not mental health
I697.summary_en: Applies a business analytics approach to school suspension data to propose a performance metric and dashboard for predicting discipline incidents and planning security resources.

I699.summary_en: Predicts suicidal tendencies in students using sixteen machine learning models (LR, NB, SVM, KNN, DT, RF, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, etc.) on the public Kaggle Student Depression Dataset. AdaBoost performs best with 84.72% cross-validation accuracy.

I700.screening_reason: Physical fitness test data, not mental health

I701.screening_reason: Outcome is academic risk and success, not mental health
I701.summary_en: Predicts academic success of Computer Science and Engineering students from Canvas LMS and Banner ERP data using Decision Trees, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, KNN and SVM. Random Forest performs best (95% accuracy), with overall GPA as the strongest indicator.

I702.screening_reason: Attention and exam integrity monitoring, not mental health
I702.summary_en: Presents a webcam-based computer vision system that monitors students' sitting posture, gaze and facial orientation during online exams to detect inattention and possible cheating. No quantitative results are reported.
